channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: Soman Chainani, Young World
channel.desc: Author Soman Chainani looks at the role of young people in American politics through his fictional novel about a teenager who becomes President of the United States.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: Q & A
channel.desc: Mollie Hemingway, editor-in-chief of The Federalist and author of Alito, discusses the life, career, and legal opinions of Supreme Court Justice Samuel Alito, who joined the Court in 2006.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: America 250
channel.desc: Author Jane Aiken discusses the events, controversies and people that shaped the history of the Library of Congress.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: Carrie Gibson, The Great Resistance
channel.desc: Author Carrie Gibson chronicles the 400-year fight to end slavery in the Americas.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: C. Evan Stewart, William Henry Seward and the Secession Winter
channel.desc: Author C. Evan Stewart discusses a little-known story about the coming of the Civil War involving William Henry Seward, later Secretary of State (1861-1869).

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: Sarah Ruden, Reproductive Wrongs - A Short History of Bad Ideas About Women
channel.desc: Historian Sarah Ruden explores how women's reproduction has been viewed throughout history. The Kansas City Public Library hosts this event.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: Matthew Mehan, The American Book of Fables
channel.desc: Hillsdale College's Matthew Mehan talks about his book of fables about American history, geography, and wildlife.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: Alvin Roth, Moral Economics
channel.desc: Author Alvin Roth examines how market principles react to some of society's most controversial transactions, including prostitution, organ sales, and drug use.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: Matthew Campbell, The Man Who Stole the Gods
channel.desc: Matthew Campbell pens a who-done-it tale about plundered Cambodian art and antiquities, the international market for stolen goods, and the sometimes unwitting participation of prominent museums.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: America's Book Club
channel.desc: Bestselling presidential historian Michael Beschloss joins David M. Rubenstein to discuss broad swaths of American history, including the Revolutionary War era, the Civil War, as well as major events of the 20th century.
